statement_or_finding: Groundnut; millet; maize; sorghum; okra; cowpea. Expert says most crops can perform in rainy season, with exceptions such as onions.
limitations_or_notes: Local expert opinion; not a quantified crop suitability trial. Verify crop, variety, planting window and Manduar farmer use. Do not treat every listed crop as confirmed in Manduar. Ask farmers about actual use, varieties, seed access and market.

statement_or_finding: Soil fertility/nitrogen status and climate variables including temperature, humidity and rainfall.
limitations_or_notes: Broad agronomic guidance. 'Virgin land' is not a sufficient soil-quality measurement; soil history and tests matter. Document as expert guidance, not a crop-specific threshold or universal prescription.

statement_or_finding: Legume followed by cereal (cowpea → maize); alternate botanical families to disrupt pest/disease cycles; combine different rooting depths.
limitations_or_notes: Nitrogen benefit depends on effective nodulation, biomass, residue retention/removal and soil conditions. Family rotation can reduce some pest/disease carryover but does not guarantee prevention. Rooting depth alone does not remediate severe compaction. Keep the explanation qualitative. Do not assign a fixed nitrogen credit or claim compaction will be broken without local evidence.

statement_or_finding: Groundnut–millet rotation is supported as a reasonable legume–cereal concept; potential fertility and pest-cycle benefits.
limitations_or_notes: Actual nitrogen carryover is conditional. Groundnut and millet response depends on variety, soil fertility, rainfall, residues and management. Treat as expert endorsement of the concept, not proof of yield improvement in Manduar.

statement_or_finding: Groundnut and cowpea are identified as nitrogen-fixing legume options.
limitations_or_notes: Biological nitrogen fixation requires effective rhizobia and suitable growing conditions. Not all fixed nitrogen remains available to the following crop. Record as general agronomic guidance; avoid stating a specific kg N/ha without a relevant source.

statement_or_finding: Cover crops/ground cover can reduce erosion and conserve moisture; ridging may help manage runoff when correctly designed.
limitations_or_notes: Effectiveness depends on species, timing, cover density, slope, soil and ridge orientation. Dry-season cover requires water and grazing protection. Compare with Manduar's reported lack of nearby dry-season water and post-harvest grazing.

statement_or_finding: Sorghum and fonio are identified by the expert as drought-resilient candidates.
limitations_or_notes: Tolerance varies by cultivar, maturity, establishment, soil and timing of drought. No rainfall threshold or variety was supplied. Record as locally informed candidate guidance; confirm seed and farmer experience in Manduar.

statement_or_finding: Soil texture/drainage and crop nutrient/water demand should inform crop choice; expert associates sandy-loamy soils with groundnut, clayey soils with rice and loamy soils with vegetables.
limitations_or_notes: These are broad tendencies, not strict crop exclusions. Manduar texture class is not confirmed; current SoilGrids data are modelled and omit silt in the extracted set. Do not classify Manduar soil from farmer wording or two fractions alone. Confirm with field texture assessment or lab.

statement_or_finding: Seed availability, labour and water are essential adoption constraints.
limitations_or_notes: Also capture cost, land access, livestock/feed needs, market/food preferences, timing and willingness to trial. Use farmer-specific constraints, not generic assumptions.

statement_or_finding: Fonio (Findi), hibiscus, cowpea and sesame identified as market opportunities.
